questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: **SENTIENT**

• "**Rhetoric**" (वक्रपटुता/शब्दआडंबर) refers to language designed to have a persuasive or impressive effect, but which is often regarded as lacking in sincerity or meaningful content. The "elasticity of rhetoric" suggests that these words are stretched to mean whatever the user wants them to mean, losing their original substance.
 
• "**Science**" (विज्ञान) is based on empirical evidence and rigid definitions. It is the opposite of "elastic" or "stretched" in the context of this critique.
 
• "**Sovereignty**" (संप्रभुता) refers to supreme power or authority. It does not fit the metaphorical description of "elasticity" or "semantic economy" discussed here.
 
• "**Urgency**" (निवार्यता/जल्दबाजी) refers to the need for immediate action. While the passage mentions planetary precarity, "urgency" is not a quality that possess "elasticity" in a linguistic sense; rather, the author argues the discourse is avoiding actual urgency.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

The advisory committee issued a set of guidelines so meticulously worded that any deviation would be tantamount ____ defiance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• Example: "His refusal to apologize was tantamount to an admission of guilt."
 
 
 
• **Common Usage:**
 
 
• This phrase is often used in formal or legal contexts.
 
• It emphasizes the gravity of a situation or action by equating it with another.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

Neither the manager nor the employees (1)/ has submitted (2)/ their performance logs (3)/ for the current quarter. (4)/
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. has submitted should be have submitted .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the correlative conjunction **"Neither...nor."** When this is used, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject closest to the verb **"has"** is **"employees,"** which is plural.
 
• Since the subject is plural, the verb must also be plural. Therefore, **"has submitted"** should be replaced with **"have submitted."**

Correct sentence: *Neither the manager nor the employees **have submitted** their performance logs for the current quarter.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement with Correlative Conjunctions:**

 
 
• When using **"either...or"** or **"neither...nor,"** the verb agrees with the nearest subject.
 
• **Example:** Either the teacher or the students **are** responsible for the decorations.
 
• If the nearest subject is singular, the verb is singular; if plural, the verb is plural.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using a singular verb with a plural subject, or vice versa, is a frequent mistake in such constructions.
 
• Always identify the nearest subject to ensure proper verb agreement.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

Historians considered the reforms emblematic of the regime's insecurity.

options.text: The reforms were emblematic of the regime's insecurity.
The reforms were considered emblematic of the regime's insecurity by historians.
The regime's insecurity was considered to be shown by reforms.
Emblematic reforms were considered part of regime insecurity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The reforms were considered emblematic of the regime's insecurity by historians. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice**, where the subject (Historians) performs the action (considered).
 
• To convert the sentence to the **passive voice**, the object of the active voice sentence (the reforms) becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• The verb is changed to the passive form using **“were considered”** (past tense of "to be" + past participle of the verb).
 
• The agent (historians) is introduced at the end of the sentence with the preposition **“by.”**

Correct sentence: *The reforms were considered emblematic of the regime's insecurity by historians*.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

A bonus will be given to all employees by the management next month.

options.text: The management gives a bonus to all employees.
The management had given a bonus to all employees.
The management will give a bonus to all employees next month.
A bonus was given by the management to all employees.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. The management will give a bonus to all employees next month .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice**.
 
• In passive voice, the subject receives the action rather than performing it.
 
• To convert the sentence into **active voice**, the subject performing the action (management) must come first, followed by the verb and then the object.
 
• In the active voice structure, the verb tense remains the same. Since the passive sentence uses "will be given," the active sentence uses "will give."

Correct sentence: *The management will give a bonus to all employees next month*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + verb + object.
 
• **Example:** The teacher explains the topic.
 
• **Usage:** Focuses on the subject performing the action.
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Object + auxiliary verb (be) + past participle + (by + subject).
 
• **Example:** The topic is explained by the teacher.
 
• **Usage:** Focuses on the action or the receiver of the action rather than the performer.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The police ***is investigating the matter seriously***.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. are investigating the matter seriously .

__
 
• The subject in the sentence is **"The police,"** which is a collective noun that is treated as plural in standard English usage.
 
• Hence, the verb should agree with the plural subject. The correct verb form is **"are"** instead of **"is"**.
 
• The correct sentence should read: **"The police are investigating the matter seriously."**
 
• Other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **Option 2:** "investigates the matter" – Incorrect because it uses the singular verb "investigates" with a plural subject.
 
• **Option 3:** "were investigating seriously the matter" – Incorrect because the tense is changed unnecessarily, and word order is awkward.
 
• **Option 4:** "is in investigation" – Incorrect because it changes the meaning and structure of the sentence.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The police **are investigating the matter seriously**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collective nouns:**
 
 
• In British English, collective nouns such as "police," "team," "family," etc., are treated as plural and take plural verbs.
 
• In American English, they are sometimes treated as singular, but "police" is always plural.
 
 
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• Always ensure the verb matches the number (singular or plural) of the subject in the sentence.

questions.question:
**A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.**

The geologist explained that tectonic shifts were inevitable.

options.text: The geologist said, "Tectonic shifts are inevitable."
"Tectonic shifts were inevitable," said the geologist.
The geologist explained, "Tectonic shifts will occur."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The geologist said, "Tectonic shifts are inevitable." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided in indirect speech is: *The geologist explained that tectonic shifts were inevitable.*
 
• To convert this into direct speech, we need to:
 
 
• Reintroduce quotation marks to enclose the words spoken by the geologist.
 
• Shift the past tense (**were**) back to the present tense (**are**), as simple present in direct speech changes to simple past in indirect speech.
 
• Identify the correct subject-speaker relationship and ensure the speaker's role is appropriately mentioned.
 
 
 
• Among the given options:
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Tectonic shifts are inevitable," uses the present simple (**are**), which correctly shifts to the past simple (**were**) in indirect speech. This is the correct answer.
 
• **Option 2:** "Tectonic shifts were inevitable," keeps the past tense, which would back-shift further to past perfect in indirect speech. This is incorrect.
 
• **Option 3:** "Tectonic shifts will occur," introduces future tense (**will occur**), which changes the meaning. This is incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "Inevitably, tectonic shifts occur," uses present simple (**occur**) and modifies the meaning, so it is also incorrect.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The geologist said, "Tectonic shifts are inevitable."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting indirect speech to direct speech:
 
 
• Ensure that the tense reflects standard back-shifting rules (e.g., past simple in indirect shifts back to present simple in direct).
 
• Quotation marks are used to enclose the exact words spoken by the subject.
 
• The reporting verb (**said, explained, etc.**) should appropriately reflect the context of the statement.
 
 
</ul
